title: French Resistance message, 1944
origin: Handwritten message sheet found with a clandestine radio set of the type used by the British SOE; shown by Didier Clarençon at HistoCrypt 2026 and published by Klaus Schmeh on 12 July 2026
observations: The first and the last group are identical (JFGEU).
Written on the sheet below the groups: 455, a five-character group that is hard to read, the count 94, and the line 'mon 20 du 5.11.44 ... NR 53 - GR 94'.
The letter counts fit French better than the other languages tested, which points to a transposition cipher; a double transposition is the usual guess for this kind of traffic.

notes: Read from the photograph of the sheet. It differs from the transcript printed with the photograph in one group: number 36 is CMENE on the sheet, not CMEME.
Group 76 is JNAAP: the writer corrected the first letter to J.
Group 38 is read as BAANO; its last letter could also be a Q.

full_solution: The keys and the complete plaintext of the message: every group from the third to the 92nd at least.

verification.how: The submitted keys are applied to the stated run of groups and must produce the submitted plaintext exactly; the plaintext must read as French, and no neighbouring key may read better.
